verses.1: Highly energetic Atikaya, who was like a mountain in form, had huge body, obtained boons from Brahma, subdued the pride of Devas and Danavas, was equal to Indra in valour. Seeing his own army of Rakshasas that caused horripilation, uncles who were bulls among Rakshasas struck down in the battlefield and his own brothers Yuddhotama (Mahodara) and Matta (Mahaparsva) struck down, he flew in rage.
verses.2: Highly energetic Atikaya, who was like a mountain in form, had huge body, obtained boons from Brahma, subdued the pride of Devas and Danavas, was equal to Indra in valour. Seeing his own army of Rakshasas that caused horripilation, uncles who were bulls among Rakshasas struck down in the battlefield and his own brothers Yuddhotama (Mahodara) and Matta (Mahaparsva) struck down, he flew in rage.
verses.3: Highly energetic Atikaya, who was like a mountain in form, had huge body, obtained boons from Brahma, subdued the pride of Devas and Danavas, was equal to Indra in valour. Seeing his own army of Rakshasas that caused horripilation, uncles who were bulls among Rakshasas struck down in the battlefield and his own brothers Yuddhotama (Mahodara) and Matta (Mahaparsva) struck down, he flew in rage.
verses.4: Adorned with a crown, Ravana glowing like a thousand suns collected together mounted the chariot and darted towards Vanaras.
verses.5: Adorned with crown, and polished earrings, twanging his bow, proclaimed his name and roared sounding aloud.
verses.6: By that lionroar, and proclamation of his name (by the sound of the twang) frightening the Vanaras he struck terror.
verses.7: Those Vanaras seeing the huge body thought, "This is Kumbhakarna, who has got up and come'. Out of fear, they sought the help of one another.
verses.8: The Vanara troops, observing his form resembling the Trivikram form assumed by Vishnu, the monkey troops fled here and there in panic.
verses.9: The Vanaras were deluded on reaching the huge body and went to Sri Rama to seek refuge.
verses.10: Then Kakutstha saw from a distance form of huge body looking like a mountain, wielding bow, rumbling like a cloud at universal destruction.
verses.11: Raghava the great, seeing the form of a huge body, was amazed, reassured by the Vanaras, and spoke to Vibheeshana.
verses.12: "Who is he, the yelloweyed, resembling a mountain, seated in the broad chariot drawn by a thousand horses?"
verses.13: "Who is he in the midst, with sharp tridents and shining spears, like Maheswara surrounded by beings?"
verses.14: "Who is he, gleaming like the tongues of time spirit (Kala spirit), with flashes of javelins, encircled with lightning and looking like a cloud shining very bright?"
verses.15: "His bows decorated with gold on the back, are like a rainbow in the sky on all sides and makes the chariot excellent."
verses.16: "The tiger among the Rakshasas seated in the chariot is the foremost car warrior. He is illuminating the battlefield like the brightness of the Sun, resplendent like Sun 's rays. By his arrows he is illuminating the ten directions. The Rahu emblem on top of the pole of the chariot is very splendid."
verses.17: "The tiger among the Rakshasas seated in the chariot is the foremost car warrior. He is illuminating the battlefield like the brightness of the Sun, resplendent like Sun 's rays. By his arrows he is illuminating the ten directions. The Rahu emblem on top of the pole of the chariot is very splendid."
verses.18: "His bow with three curves, covered with gold, decorated, is close to a thundering cloud, casting its splendour."
verses.19: "His chariot with standard, flag and axletree is a great one driven by four charioteers emitting sound like the rumblings of clouds."
verses.20: "This chariot has twenty quivers, ten frightening bows, and eight bow strings of golden colour lay arranged in the chariot."
verses.21: "It has two swords off our cubits and ten cubits long swords provided with hilts hanging on its sides as decoration."
verses.22: "Wearing red garland s round the neck, brave, like a mountain in form, dark with large mouth, like death, like sun veiled by clouds he seems."
verses.23: "By adorning armlets, his both arms are like high peaks of Himalaya mountain shining away."
verses.24: "He who shines like the full moon between two Punarvasu stars, his auspicious eyes and countenance shines with both earrings."
verses.25: "Oh! Vibheeshana, a mighty armed one! Show me that foremost of Rakshasas, whom all Vanaras feared and fled in all directions."
verses.26: Interrogated by the highly brilliant prince Raghava, energetic Vibheeshana revealed.
verses.27: "The tenheaded and highly brilliant king Ravana, who is the brother of Vysravana, is of terrible deeds and highly exploitative."
verses.28: "To him was born a blessed son, valiant one, compeer of Ravana, who served elders, learned and well versed in sastras."
verses.29: "He is best in riding on horseback, on elephant back and in the use of sword and bow. He is capable of sowing dissension, making peace, giving charity and statecraft."
verses.30: "He is known as Atikaya, son of Dhanyamalini. Lanka remains fearless on his shoulders, you may know."
verses.31: "By penance on supreme self he propitiated Brahma, who blessed him with mystic missiles by way of boons by which his enemies were subdued."
verses.32: "Exemption from death from gods and demons was given to him and all this wonderful shield and chariot as bright as the sun."
verses.33: "By this (boon) hundreds of Devatas and demons were defeated by him, Yakshas were killed, nay Rakshasas were protected."
verses.34: "Here is strong Atikaya, a wise son of Ravana, bull among Rakshasas, who is a subduer of the pride of Devas and Danavas, by whom thunderbolt of Indra was obstructed firmly in battle and likewise the noose of Varuna was repelled in war."
verses.35: "Here is strong Atikaya, a wise son of Ravana, bull among Rakshasas, who is a subduer of the pride of Devas and Danavas, by whom thunderbolt of Indra was obstructed firmly in battle and likewise the noose of Varuna was repelled in war."
verses.36: "Oh, best of men! Quickly make efforts to put an end to him before he puts down Vanara army."
verses.37: Thereafter, mighty Atikaya entered the monkey army, twanged his bow again and again and made a loud noise.
verses.38: Observing the dreadful enemy seated on the chariot, the foremost of the great Vanaras rushed towards him.
verses.39: Kumuda, Dwivida, Mainda, Neela, even Sarabha, all at once assailed him with trees and mountain peaks.
verses.40: Atikaya, endowed with extraordinary energy, efficient in the use of weapons, shattered the trees and rocks hurled by the Vanaras with his arrows adorned with gold.
verses.41: The powerful night ranger of terrible form, pierced all monkeys who were facing him in the battlefield with iron arrows.
verses.42: The monkeys were hard pressed by Atikaya's hail of arrows. Their limbs broke and were unable to resist.
verses.43: Just as a young lion with youthful pride would strike a group of deer, the enraged Rakshasa struck the army of monkey heroes.
verses.44: The Rakshasa lord, wielding a weapon in the midst of the monkey army, indeed did not strike any, but armed with bow and quiver went with pride towards Rama and spoke.
verses.45: "I am with a bow and arrow seated in the chariot. Indeed, I am not strong in fighting with common warriors. Whoever is interested to fight now can come speedily to fight with me."
verses.46: On hearing Atikaya, Saumithri the destroyer of enemies, became angry, not enduring and not able to tolerate went towards him taking a sword.
verses.47: Furious Saumithri, springing up, took up his arrow from the quiver, stretching to full length before he discharged the arrow.
verses.48: The twang of Lakshmana filled the mountains, earth, ocean, and all directions striking terrible fear in the night ranger.
verses.49: Then the extraordinarily energetic and powerful son of Rakshasa king was in turn frightened at the sound of Saumithri's bow and was astonished.
verses.50: Seeing Atikaya, furious Lakshmana sprang up and took a sharp shaft and spoke as follows.
verses.51: "O Saumithri! You are valiant but young, not able to discriminate. I am equal to the Lord of death. Why do you desire to comb at with me?"
verses.52: The shafts discharged from my arm can't be borne, by the Himalayas, even the atmosphere between the sky and earth can't bear the force.
verses.53: "Why do you want to arouse the fire of dissolution sleeping comfortably? Return, casting away your bow, without confronting. Go away."
verses.54: "Or else if you want to oppose and not return, give up your life and proceed to Yama's abode."
verses.55: "See my sharp shafts capable of reducing enemy's pride like Ishwara's trident, ornamented with polished gold."
verses.56: "These arrows are like serpents and can drink your blood just as an angry lion drinks the blood of elephants. Therefore, I tell you", said Atikaya to Lakshmana."
verses.57: Prince Atikaya, having spoken as said before, fitted his bow in wrath. Hearing the proud statement of Atikaya, the highminded Lakshmana, endowed with strength, enraged, and spoke these words of great meaning.
verses.58: "You are evil minded. By mere statement you people can't become good chiefs. I stand armed with a bow and arrow. Prove your strength."
verses.59: "Reveal yourself by action not by indication. You do not deserve it. He who is with prowess is a right hero."
verses.60: "You are seated in the chariot with all kinds of weapons collected. By that alone you do not become capable. Show your capacity."
verses.61: "Then I will strike down his head with sharp arrows and throw him just as ripened palm fruit drops in the process of time."
verses.62: "Now, you will drink the blood ejected from your neck by the holes made with my pointed arrows decked with polished gold."
